label: Jon T. Kosloski
narrative: Kosloski is the third person to run AARO and the first whose tenure produced anything the disclosure side counts as movement. He came from the National Security Agency, where he was a senior research scientist working in quantum optics, cryptanalysis and advanced research; DoD announced his selection on 26 August 2024, ending nine months in which the office had no confirmed director. His public line is materially identical to Kirkpatrick's on the central question - 'to date, AARO has discovered no verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial beings, activity, or technology,' as he told the Senate Armed Services Emerging Threats and Capabilities Subcommittee on 19 November 2024 - but his framing diverges in two ways that matter. He has repeatedly conceded that a residue of cases is 'truly anomalous' and that there are cases he does not understand, and he has committed the office to declassification and data-sharing rather than pure debunking. At his 14 November 2024 media roundtable on the FY2024 report he disclosed the GREMLIN prototype sensor system undergoing a 90-day collection at a classified national security site, described AARO as employing several dozen personnel, and promised Volume II of the Historical Record Report 'within months' - a promise that as of August 2026 remains unkept. He signed off on the FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report, which reached Congress on 21 July 2026, months past the statutory cycle in 50 U.S.C. 3373(k), and which carries the most striking single case AARO has ever published: roughly 100 airborne UAP and two likely uncrewed surface systems observed by US Navy assets off the Virginia coast, still unresolved. In May 2026 he met Reps. Anna Paulina Luna and Tim Burchett and, per Luna, apologised for the conduct of the prior AARO leadership - after which Luna, who had spent more than a year demanding the office be defunded, publicly backed him. That apology is the closest thing to an institutional admission that the Kirkpatrick-era office behaved improperly toward Congress and witnesses.
